description: baseline

Target n=4096 batch-2 dominance by replacing the CholeskyQR reconstruction path with a blocked multi-CTA Householder-to-compact reconstruction that avoids forming full Q in global memory and reduces triangular solve/reconstruction launch overhead.

Routed B=2 n=4096 to existing compact Householder large_n path to avoid CholeskyQR reconstruction; build passed but validation guards failed/timed out after n4096 differential guard hit CUDA invalid argument.
Routed B=2 n=4096 to torch.geqrf as a library compact-Householder baseline. It validates but benchmark regresses because n4096 shape rises to 54508.549 us and geomean to 2507.514 us.

Tried widening CholeskyQR orhr_col recon LU outer block to 128 to reduce solve/reconstruction overhead. Main tests passed, but diff guard found n4096 orthogonality residual 0.0887 > 0.0488 on one distinct input.
Tried widening CholeskyQR right-solve block to nb=448 to reduce per-block solve/reconstruction launch overhead. Validation passed, but benchmark n4096 failed orthogonality residual 0.0615 > 0.0488.
Tried safer CholeskyQR right-solve block nb=320. It validates and keeps n4096 correct, but benchmark regresses to 2257.925 us versus parent 2251.432; n4096 shape is 15370.064 us.

Exhausted brief 0. Best valid attempt was the parent baseline at 2251.432 us; no attempted compact-Householder/reconstruction change beat it. Direct existing blocked Householder dispatch failed n4096 guard with CUDA invalid argument, torch.geqrf validated but regressed to 2507.514 us, LU outer=128 failed diff guard orthogonality, TRSM nb=448 passed validation but failed benchmark orthogonality, and safer nb=320 validated but regressed to 2257.925 us. Final branch HEAD is nb=320 (18c7c968) with nsys and ncu profiles saved; next brief should likely target a genuinely new multi-CTA compact reconstruction kernel rather than knob changes to the current CholeskyQR/orhr_col path.

Target n=4096 batch-2 again from baseline, but implement a genuinely new compact reconstruction kernel: apply Householder vectors directly to form LAPACK H/tau from Cholesky Q/R using row-slab CTAs and avoid torch.geqrf/current TRSM knob paths entirely.
Implemented a distinct compact reconstruction path by geqrf-factorizing Cholesky Q and splicing in Cholesky R. It validates but is far slower: n4096 shape 62985.221 us and geomean 2548.898 us.

Tried using the existing custom blocked_qr on Cholesky Q to produce compact H/tau, then splice in R. Main tests passed but diff guard failed with cublas errors and CUDA misaligned address during n4096 distinct-input checks.

Added a new CUDA direct_compact_from_Q kernel that derives H/tau columns from Cholesky Q and splices R, avoiding orhr_col LU. Build and main tests passed, but diff guard rejected n4096 because the pybind vector return surfaced as a list rather than required tuple.

Fixed direct_compact_from_Q to return a Python tuple. The new direct reflector extraction still fails diff guard for n4096: R - Q.T @ A residual around 1.36e3 versus allowed about 32, so the column-local reflector extraction is not algebraically equivalent to LAPACK compact H.
Tried flipping the diagonal sign convention in direct_compact_from_Q. It still fails n4096 diff guard with R - Q.T @ A residual about 1.4e3, so the direct per-column extraction remains invalid.

Exhausted brief 1. Best score remains parent baseline 2251.432 us. A genuinely different QR-of-Cholesky-Q compact reconstruction validated but was much slower at 2548.898 us (n4096 62985.221 us). Existing custom blocked_qr-on-Q failed with cublas/misaligned errors. The new direct_compact_from_Q CUDA kernel compiled and main tests passed, but after fixing tuple return it failed n4096 diff guard with R-Q.T@A residual ~1.36e3; flipping sign still failed ~1.4e3. Final HEAD is the only valid QR-based reconstruction commit 6d335b8c, with NCU profile saved. Next brief should derive the exact LAPACK compact reflectors via a dependency-aware blocked WY/orhr_col replacement rather than independent column reflectors from Q.

Target n=4096 batch-2 from baseline by replacing orhr_col with a dependency-aware blocked WY compact-reflector generator: compute each panel of Householder vectors from Cholesky Q using triangular block solves, then emit LAPACK H/tau without forming per-column independent reflectors.

Tried dependency-aware reconstruction using torch.linalg.lu_factor_ex(pivot=False) on M=Q-D, then building H/tau from LU and R. Main tests passed, but diff guard failed on n4096 with CUDA launch out-of-resources in torch no-pivot LU.

Tried looped per-matrix torch.linalg.lu_factor_ex(pivot=False) to avoid batched out-of-resources and generate compact reflectors from M=Q-D. It builds and main tests pass, but n4096 diff guard fails orthogonality on 6/8 distinct inputs.
Tried dependency-aware baseline orhr_col with smaller LU/WY panel block bs=32. It validates but is slower: n4096 shape 16445.787 us and geomean 2270.292 us versus parent 2251.432.

Exhausted brief 2. Best score remains parent baseline 2251.432 us. torch lu_factor_ex(pivot=False) on the full batch failed n4096 diff guard with launch out-of-resources; looped per-matrix torch no-pivot LU avoided that but failed orthogonality on 6/8 distinct n4096 inputs. The only valid dependency-aware variant was the existing orhr_col/WY path with smaller bs=32, but it regressed to 2270.292 us (n4096 16445.787 us). Final HEAD is 5a95ed93 with NCU profile saved. The baseline bs=64 C++ orhr_col remains the best tested dependency-aware compact generator.

Combine the leading n=512 split-dispatch win with the best n=32 Python early-dispatch path, resolve any submission.py conflicts, and verify whether the shape-specific fast paths stack without hurting mixed n=512 behavior.

Combined n512 split-dispatch parent b5f78f1d with tiny Python early-dispatch parent bbca8302. Resolved function-list and custom_kernel conflicts; validation passed. Benchmark improves to 2234.579 us; mixed n512 shape improves to 7405.547 us while n32 remains 10.288 us.

Exhausted combine brief 3. Integrated both parents b5f78f1d (n512 split-dispatch) and bbca8302 (n32 Python early dispatch), resolving submission.py conflicts by keeping compact_n512_bad_input in the extension function list and adding the early tiny return in custom_kernel. Validation and guards passed. Benchmark improved to 2234.579 us versus baseline 2251.432; mixed n512 behavior improved strongly (shape 7 7405.547 us) and n32 stayed fast at 10.288 us. NCU on mixed n512 timed out, so an nsys profile was captured for the combined commit 0d27a2d1.

Combine the new n=1024 exact-route win b1ca555b with the n=512 split plus n=1024 rblk2 combined best 9ac867b9, resolve dispatch conflicts, and benchmark whether the top-share n512 and n1024 improvements stack without regressing n2048/n4096.

Combined b1ca555b n1024 exact-route with full 9ac867b9 n512 split + n1024 rblk2 changes. Validation passed. Benchmark improves to 2186.683 us; n512 shapes improve (dense 3759.576, mixed 7385.131), n1024 exact-route shapes are 4665.815/4671.488/4660.224, and n2048/n4096 remain comparable at 8923.296/15265.792.

Exhausted combine brief 4. Integrated b1ca555b n=1024 exact-route with the full 9ac867b9 n=512 split + n=1024 rblk2 best by taking the full 9ac867b9 tree and re-applying the B==60 exact-route guard. Validation/guards passed. Benchmark improved to 2186.683 us; n512 dense/mixed are 3759.576/7385.131, n1024 shapes are 4665.815/4671.488/4660.224, and n2048/n4096 remain comparable at 8923.296/15265.792. Final commit 2c67c418 has an nsys profile for n1024 mixed saved.

Extend current best 2c67c418 and target n1024 runtime by adding a cheap device classifier that routes only mixed/hard B=60 n1024 batches to the exact FP32 path, while restoring fast FP16+rblk2 for dense and nearrank n1024 shapes to recover their regressions.

Added cheap B=60 n1024 device classifier: all-good dense/nearrank batches route to FP16+rblk2, any detected hard/mixed matrix keeps exact FP32. Validation/guards passed; benchmark improves to 2115.742 us with n1024 dense/nearrank 3777.255/3779.444 us and mixed 4698.572 us.

Tried per-matrix split for B=60 n1024 mixed batches: good matrices run FP16+rblk2 and bad matrices exact FP32, then index-copy merged. Validation passed but benchmark regressed to 2216.451 us because n1024 mixed slowed to 8032.246 us from extra copies plus underfilled exact/fast sub-batches.

Tried reducing B=60 n1024 classifier overhead by suppressing good-count atomics when good_idx is null. Validation passed but benchmark regressed to 2191.439 us: the count-only expression aliases good matrices into counts[0], so dense/nearrank B=60 route exact FP32 again (~4699/4693 us).

Exhausted brief 5. Best commit is c430d3ae, adding a cheap B=60 n=1024 device classifier that restores FP16+rblk2 for all-good dense/nearrank batches while keeping any detected hard/mixed batch on exact FP32. Validation and guards passed; best benchmark is 2115.742 us versus parent 2186.683 us, with n1024 dense/nearrank improved to 3777.255/3779.444 us and mixed preserved near exact at 4698.572 us. Tried per-matrix mixed splitting (6f87acf4) but it regressed to 2216.451 us from copy/underfilled sub-batch overhead; tried count-only good suppression (34e36eb8) but it misrouted dense/nearrank exact and regressed to 2191.439 us. Final nsys profile saved for c430d3ae on n1024 dense.

Combine current best c430d3ae with build-time setter-pruning win b5e0d3c0, resolve source conflicts, and verify whether the n1024 classifier speedup stacks with lower compile surface without regressing high-share shapes.

Attempted to combine b5e0d3c0 setter-pruning with c430d3ae n1024 classifier by hardwiring constant setters while preserving compact_large_bad_input. Wrapped build returned code 124 after acquiring the build lock with no compiler diagnostics, so logging before retry/fix.

Recovered combine after transient lock/cache build timeout: de8fe33d hardwires b5e0d3c0 constant setters while preserving c430d3ae n1024 classifier. Build passed on retry, validation/guards passed, benchmark is 2129.884 us; runtime is slightly slower than c430d3ae 2115.742 but preserves the n1024 dense/nearrank FP16 route and reduces exported setter surface.

Exhausted combine brief 6. Integrated b5e0d3c0 build-time setter pruning into current best c430d3ae while preserving the B=60 n1024 classifier and compact_large_bad_input export. First build attempt de8fe33d was logged as build_error because the wrapped build timed out during fleet/cache contention; the same commit later built successfully after lock contention cleared, validation/guards passed, and benchmark scored 2129.884 us. This is slightly slower than c430d3ae 2115.742, but it preserves the major n1024 dense/nearrank FP16 route (n1024 dense 3805.682 us, nearrank 3778.133 us, mixed 4724.829 us) while reducing compile/export setter surface. Final nsys profile saved for de8fe33d. Recommendation: keep c430d3ae for pure runtime best; use de8fe33d only if build/compile surface is prioritized.

Extend current best c430d3ae and target the two largest remaining runtime shares n4096 batch-2 and n2048 batch-8 by tuning existing CholeskyQR/blocked-QR internals: Ozaki/Gram accumulation, triangular solve/reconstruction, and row-block thresholds to reduce high-share runtime while preserving compact H/tau correctness and build time.

Tried lowering _CHOLQR_MIN_N from 4096 to 2048 to route n2048 B=8 through existing Ozaki/CholeskyQR/reconstruction internals. Build passed, but validation failed on n2048 mixed: Q orth residual 0.0261 > allowed 0.0244 (scaled 107), so this route is not safe without additional hardening.

Tried widening _TRSM_NB_CPP from 384 to 448 for n4096 CholeskyQR triangular solve. Build and validation passed, but benchmark correctness failed on active n4096 B=2 seed 32412: orth residual 0.0615 > allowed 0.0488 (scaled 126), confirming this block width lacks enough margin.

Tried widening _LARGE_HI FP16 blocked-QR from OB/IB 48/24 to 64/32 for n2048 B=8. Main validation tests passed, but diff_correctness_guard hit CUDA invalid argument during later active-shape checks, so the panel-width route is not safe.

Tried pruning Ozaki Gram products by lowering _OZ_MAXPQ from 4 to 3 for n4096 CholeskyQR. Main tests passed with low residuals, but diff_correctness_guard failed on n4096 B=2 because Cholesky became non-PD (leading minor 4095), so the Gram pruning loses required robustness.

Tried widening reconstruction LU outer panel _LU_OUTER from 64 to 128 while keeping _LU_BLOCK=64 for n4096 CholeskyQR/orhr_col reconstruction. Main tests passed, but diff_correctness_guard failed n4096 B=2 on a distinct seed (orth residual 0.0887 > allowed 0.0488), so the reconstruction threshold lacks robustness.

Exhausted brief 7. No valid improvement over current best c430d3ae was found for the n4096/n2048 internals. Tried n2048 CholeskyQR threshold (_CHOLQR_MIN_N=2048, ec072bd2): validation failed n2048 mixed orthogonality. Tried n4096 TRSM block width 448 (1bd59b81): validation passed but active benchmark n4096 seed failed orthogonality. Tried n2048 blocked-QR OB/IB 64/32 (83ff94c2): main tests passed but diff guard hit CUDA invalid argument. Tried Ozaki Gram pair pruning _OZ_MAXPQ=3 (3566a3a3): guard failed with non-PD Cholesky on n4096. Tried reconstruction LU outer panel 128 (08bab752): guard failed n4096 distinct seed orthogonality. Final HEAD restored to c430d3ae; recommendation is to keep current n4096 CholeskyQR settings (OZ_MAXPQ=4, TRSM_NB=384, LU ob/bs=64) and current n2048 blocked-QR settings (OB/IB 48/24).

Extend new best 26620c5b and target high-share n2048 batch-8 with a new blocked-QR dataflow: specialize the panel/trailing update for small batch count by fusing panel factorization, compact H/tau emission, and trailing update to reduce launch/scratch overhead without using the failed CholeskyQR route.

Enabled existing BF16 panel+apply fused dataflow for n2048 by switching _LARGE_HI IB 24->16 and setting inner_wmma=2/panel_apply_fused=1/paf_no_csh. Validation/guards passed, but benchmark regressed to 2138.079 us; n2048 B=8 slowed to 9925.861 us, so extra panels/launches outweighed fused inner applies.

Tried enabling _LARGE_HI ov_fold=1 to fuse n2048 outer-V emission into panel writeback without changing OB/IB. Build passed but validation failed on n2048: dense/rankdef produced NaN/Inf H and mixed had large factor residual, so the fold path is invalid for current n2048 wsp/cm-coop panel.

Tried wide n2048 panel+apply fused dataflow with _LARGE_HI OB/IB 64/32 plus inner_wmma=2/panel_apply_fused=1/paf_no_csh=1. Build passed but validation failed in diff_correctness_guard: n2048 B=8 distinct inputs produced H NaN/Inf, so this fused wide-panel route is invalid.

Tried n2048 small-batch panel+apply fused dataflow with _LARGE_HI IB 16, inner_wmma=2, paf_warps=16 and paf_no_csh=1. Validation and guards passed, but benchmark regressed to 2133.222 us; n2048 B=8 remained slow at 9917.355 us, so lower-occupancy fusion still loses to parent launch/dataflow balance.

Tried n2048 small-batch panel+apply fused dataflow with _LARGE_HI IB 16, inner_wmma=2, paf_warps=32 and staged Csh. Validation and guards passed, and it was the best valid fused variant, but benchmark still regressed to 2132.133 us with n2048 B=8 at 9911.227 us; fusion overhead and extra inner panels do not beat parent OB/IB 48/24.

Exhausted brief 8. No valid improvement over new best 26620c5b was found for n2048 B=8 blocked-QR fused dataflow. Tested existing panel+apply fusion on _LARGE_HI with IB 16/paf_no_csh (5d4ac0b): valid but slower at 2138.079 us and n2048 9925.861 us. Tested ov_fold=1 (5c4d6b5): invalid with H NaN/Inf and mixed residual failure. Tested wide OB/IB 64/32 fused (1ae1e8b): invalid in diff_correctness_guard with n2048 H NaN/Inf. Tested lower-occupancy IB16 paf_warps=16 no_csh (96b9812): valid but slower at 2133.222 us, n2048 9917.355 us. Tested staged-Csh IB16 paf_warps=32 (16271fb): best valid fused variant but still slower at 2132.133 us, n2048 9911.227 us. Final HEAD restored to 26620c5b; recommendation is to keep parent _LARGE_HI OB/IB 48/24 without panel_apply_fused/ov_fold for n2048.

Extend current best 8975f743 and revisit FP8 with a true fused tensor-core path: replace split Wq/Wr residual GEMMs with a custom/cublasLt-style scaled FP8 trailing GEMM plus fused residual epilogue for n1024 dense/nearrank, avoiding extra launches and preserving mixed exact routing.

Tried replacing the split n1024 FP8 W residual GEMM with a custom fused residual-Y epilogue kernel after M*Wq. Build passed and regular tests passed, but diff_correctness_guard failed n1024 dense/nearrank cases with factor residuals above tolerance, so the custom per-element residual accumulation order is not numerically safe.

Tried a cublasGemmStridedBatchedEx n1024 W path using CUDA_R_8F_E4M3 for Wq, replacing the split Wq/Wr residual GEMMs with a single FP8-input Y GEMM. Build and regular tests passed, but validation guards failed n1024 dense/nearrank with very large factor residuals and cuBLAS status 15 reports, so this cublas FP8 operand path is not safe/supported in this layout.

Exhausted brief 9. Starting from current best 8975f743, revisited FP8 for n1024 B=60 with true fused/non-split directions rather than the prior Wq/Wr split residual GEMMs. Attempt 7c470942 added a custom fused residual-Y epilogue after M*Wq to replace the second residual GEMM; build and regular tests passed, but diff_correctness_guard failed n1024 dense/nearrank with factor residuals above tolerance, so the custom per-element residual accumulation order is not numerically safe. Attempt d851289a used cublasGemmStridedBatchedEx with CUDA_R_8F_E4M3 Wq for a single FP8-input Y GEMM; build and regular tests passed, but guards failed n1024 dense/nearrank with very large residuals and cuBLAS status 15 reports, so that cublas FP8 operand layout/support is invalid here. No valid fused FP8 improvement was found; final HEAD restored to 8975f743. Recommendation: keep current best and do not land split residual FP8 on this parent; future FP8 work needs a proper cublasLt matmul descriptor with scales/amax or a tensor-core kernel that preserves the split residual accumulation order.

Extend current best 8975f743 and target Python/C++ dispatch overhead across low-share small shapes only if it does not distract from high-share paths: create a consolidated fast-return path for n32/n176/n352 that avoids extension import work and redundant scratch allocation, preserving high-share runtime/build behavior.

Replaced the per-call predicate/lambda dispatch table with an equivalent direct branch ladder, targeting low-share n32/n176/n352 Python dispatch overhead while preserving all existing kernel handlers and high-share routes. Build and validation/guards passed, but benchmark regressed to 2116.707 us, likely from noise/no high-share benefit; not better than parent 8975f743.

Added a dedicated n176 FP32 small-shape path that bypasses the generic small-n setup/dict lookups and directly applies the existing tuned WSP/cm/blk4 settings before blocked_qr, leaving n352 BF16 and all high-share n512/n1024/n2048/n4096 routes unchanged. Build and validation/guards passed; benchmark improved to 2108.902 us with high-share timings preserved within noise.

Stacked a custom_kernel n32 shortcut on top of the valid n176 fast path so tiny shape bypasses _custom_kernel_generic. Validation and guards passed, but benchmark regressed to 2112.548 us versus n176-only 2108.902; n32 was unchanged and high-share noise/regression outweighed any Python-call savings.

Exhausted brief 10. Best result is afd3105b: a dedicated n176 FP32 small-shape fast path that bypasses the generic small-n setup/dict lookups and directly applies the existing tuned WSP/cm/blk4 settings before blocked_qr. It preserves n352 BF16 and all high-share n512/n1024/n2048/n4096 routes. Build and full validation/guards passed; benchmark improved to 2108.902 us versus parent 8975f743. Other attempts: aeb4db83 direct dispatch ladder validated but regressed to 2116.707, and d4e5479d n32 custom_kernel shortcut stacked on afd3105b validated but regressed to 2112.548. Final HEAD left at afd3105b; recommendation is to keep n176-only fast path and avoid the n32 shortcut/direct ladder.

Combine previous best 8975f743 with new n176 fast-path best afd3105b, preserving n512 one-pass classifier/parallel compile and adopting only the n176 FP32 fast path if validation and active geomean stay improved.

Combined current best 8975f743 with afd3105b by applying only the dedicated n176 FP32 fast path. The diff is limited to _qr_small_n176_fp32 plus the n==176 dispatch call, preserving n512 one-pass classifier/parallel compile and all high-share routes. Build and validation/guards passed; benchmark scored 2110.660 us, improved versus 8975f743 and within expected noise of afd3105b.

Exhausted brief 11. Final candidate c11b30cb combines previous best 8975f743 with afd3105b by adopting only the n176 FP32 fast path: _qr_small_n176_fp32 plus the n==176 dispatch call. It preserves the n512 one-pass classifier/parallel compile and does not include the rejected direct ladder or n32 shortcut. Build passed, full validation and problem guards passed, and active benchmark scored 2110.660 us, improved over parent 8975f743 and consistent with afd3105b within benchmark noise. Recommendation: keep c11b30cb as the combined n176-only fast-path candidate.

Extend current best 4d0aab26 and target small-shape n176/n352 dispatch overhead by generalizing the n176 fast path only if it composes with the msplit prune: add a guarded n352 fast path or shared small-shape dispatcher, but keep all high-share n512/n1024/n2048/n4096 routes unchanged.

Added guarded n176 FP32 and n352 BF16 small-shape fast paths on top of msplit-pruned parent 4d0aab26 without reintroducing msplit exports or touching n512/n1024/n2048/n4096 routes. Build and validation/guards passed, but active benchmark scored 2113.063 us; n352 fast path did not improve enough and high-share noise made it worse than desired.

Added only the n176 FP32 fast path on msplit-pruned parent 4d0aab26, without reintroducing msplit exports or touching n512/n1024/n2048/n4096 routes. Build and validation/guards passed, but active benchmark scored 2113.870 us, so the small-shape dispatch saving did not improve geomean on this parent.

Exhausted brief 12. Best final remains parent 4d0aab26: both small-shape generalizations validated but did not improve the active geomean on the msplit-pruned base. Commit 464ba374 added guarded n176+n352 fast paths and scored 2113.063 us; commit 2bfd8ac1 kept only the n176 FP32 fast path and scored 2113.870 us. Both preserved high-share n512/n1024/n2048/n4096 routes and did not reintroduce msplit exports, but neither composed into an improvement; final HEAD reset to 4d0aab26 and a final n352 profile was captured. Recommendation: keep 4d0aab26 and avoid n352/n176-only dispatch changes on this parent unless a later brief targets a deeper shared dispatcher.

Extend current best 4d0aab26 and do a narrow n2048 B=8 blocked-QR parameter sweep around the known-safe OB/IB 48/24 settings: test only local constants that do not change dataflow, stopping on any validation instability.

Narrow n2048 B=8 local parameter sweep candidate: changed only _LARGE_HI FP16 blocked-QR OB/IB from 48/24 to 40/20, preserving dataflow and all other flags. Build and validation/guards passed, but benchmark regressed to 2130.505 us with n2048 shape at 9893.413 us, so this narrower panel is worse.

Narrow n2048 B=8 local parameter sweep candidate: changed only _LARGE_HI FP16 blocked-QR OB/IB from 48/24 to 56/28, preserving the same two-inner-panel dataflow and all other flags. Build and validation/guards passed; benchmark scored 2120.841 us with n2048 at 9261.728 us, better than 40/20 but still not an active-geomean improvement.

Narrow n2048 B=8 local parameter sweep candidate: changed only _LARGE_HI FP16 blocked-QR OB/IB from 48/24 to nearby 52/26, preserving two-inner-panel dataflow and all other flags. Build and validation/guards passed, but benchmark regressed to 2147.384 us with n2048 at 10899.968 us; this exceeds the safe local optimum.

Narrow n2048 B=8 local parameter sweep candidate: kept OB/IB at known-safe 48/24 and changed only _LARGE_HI bf16_nt from 576 to 512. Build and validation/guards passed; benchmark scored 2112.261 us with n2048 at 8933.136 us, the best sweep point so far but not clearly better than parent/current best under whole-active geomean noise.

Narrow n2048 B=8 local parameter sweep candidate: kept OB/IB at known-safe 48/24 and changed only _LARGE_HI bf16_nt from 576 to 640. Build and validation/guards passed; benchmark scored 2112.211 us with n2048 at 8928.400 us, essentially tied with bf16_nt=512 and better n2048 shape time, but whole-active geomean is not a decisive improvement over parent.

Narrow n2048 B=8 local parameter sweep candidate: kept OB/IB at known-safe 48/24 and changed only _LARGE_HI minv_nt from 640 to 512. Build and validation/guards passed; benchmark scored 2111.723 us with n2048 at 8931.626 us, the best full active-geomean point so far in this sweep.

Narrow n2048 B=8 local parameter sweep candidate: kept known-safe OB/IB 48/24 and combined bf16_nt=640 with minv_nt=512, preserving dataflow and all other high-share routes. Build and validation/guards passed; benchmark scored 2110.167 us with n2048 at 8898.160 us, the best point in brief 13.

Exhausted brief 13 n2048 B=8 local constant sweep around OB/IB 48/24. Best candidate is c2dc1f44: it preserves the known-safe 48/24 blocked-QR dataflow and changes only _LARGE_HI bf16_nt 576->640 plus minv_nt 640->512. Build and full validation/guards passed, benchmark scored 2110.167 us with n2048 at 8898.160 us, and a final n2048 NCU profile was captured. Other validated sweep points were worse: OB40/IB20 2130.505, OB56/IB28 2120.841, OB52/IB26 2147.384, bf16_nt512 2112.261, bf16_nt640 2112.211, minv_nt512 2111.723. Recommendation: keep c2dc1f44 as the best local micro-tune; avoid moving OB/IB off 48/24.
Combine current best 4d0aab26 with n2048 local micro-tune c2dc1f44, preserving msplit prune and adopting only bf16_nt=640 plus minv_nt=512 if validation and benchmark improve.

Combined current best 4d0aab26 with c2dc1f44 by adopting only the _LARGE_HI n2048 local constants bf16_nt=640 and minv_nt=512. This preserves msplit prune/build surface, keeps OB/IB at 48/24 and leaves high-share routes/dataflow unchanged. Build and full validation/guards passed; benchmark improved to 2109.510 us with n2048 at 8893.595 us.

Exhausted brief 14 combine. Final candidate afb5709c combines current best 4d0aab26 with the c2dc1f44 n2048 local micro-tune by adopting only _LARGE_HI bf16_nt=640 and minv_nt=512. It preserves the msplit prune/build surface, keeps OB/IB at known-safe 48/24, and does not alter n512/n1024/n4096 routes or dataflow. Build and full validation/guards passed; active benchmark improved to 2109.510 us with n2048 at 8893.595 us. Final n2048 NCU profile captured. Recommendation: keep afb5709c as the combined best.

Extend current best 4d0aab26 and target n2048 B=8 by replacing the current fixed panel schedule with a runtime-adaptive two-panel schedule that uses the proven 48/24 path for hard matrices and a lighter 56/28 or bf16_nt/minv_nt-tuned path only for dense/well-conditioned matrices, preserving compact H/tau correctness.

Added a runtime-adaptive n2048 B=8 path using compact_large_bad_input: dense/well-conditioned batches take the tuned 48/24 schedule with bf16_nt=640,minv_nt=512, while hard matrices stay on the proven 48/24 base schedule and mixed batches split/scatter H/tau. Build and validation/guards passed, but benchmark scored 2110.310 us with n2048 at 8943.120 us; classifier overhead made it worse than the fixed tuned path.

Added runtime-adaptive n2048 B=8 schedule using compact_large_bad_input where dense/well-conditioned matrices take a lighter OB56/IB28 path and hard matrices stay on the proven OB48/IB24 path. Build and validation/guards passed, but benchmark regressed to 2120.773 us with n2048 at 9271.072 us, confirming OB56/IB28 is not a useful dense branch.

Exhausted brief 15. Runtime-adaptive n2048 B=8 two-panel schedules validated, but neither improved the active benchmark.
